events.title: Abu al-Abbas holds a victory parade in Baghdad after the Zanj Rebellion
events.description: Abu al-Abbas, the future caliph al-Mu'tadid, held a victory parade in Baghdad after the Zanj Rebellion. The revolt in southern Iraq, led by Ali ibn Muhammad and involving enslaved and freed Africans, had ended with the fall of al-Mukhtarah in August.

events.title: Edmund Ironside dies, leaving Cnut king of all England
events.description: Edmund II died weeks after agreeing to divide England with the Danish king Cnut. Cnut became sole king, later also ruling Denmark and Norway in a North Sea empire.

events.title: Jonathan Swift is born in Dublin
events.description: Jonathan Swift, later Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, was born. His Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal made him one of the great satirists in English.
events.html: Jonathan Swift, later Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, was born. His Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal made him one of the great satirists in English.

events.title: Charles XII's Swedish troops rout the Russian army at Narva
events.description: About 8,000 Swedish troops under King Charles XII routed a Russian army three to four times their size that was besieging Narva, early in the Great Northern War. The defeat prompted Peter I's reforms, which gave Russia a standing professional army.

events.title: Samuel Clemens, later Mark Twain, is born
events.description: Samuel Langhorne Clemens was born in Florida, Missouri. As Mark Twain he wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, drawing on his boyhood on the Mississippi.

events.title: Scotland and England play the first international football match
events.description: Scotland and England drew 0-0 at Hamilton Crescent in Partick, Glasgow, before about 4,000 spectators. It is recognised by FIFA as the first official international football match.
events.html: Scotland and England drew 0-0 at Hamilton Crescent in Partick, Glasgow, before about 4,000 spectators. It is recognised by FIFA as the first official international football match.

events.title: The Soviet Union invades Finland
events.description: Soviet forces attacked Finland, starting the Winter War. Fierce Finnish resistance inflicted heavy losses before Finland ceded territory in March 1940, and the Red Army's poor showing was noted in Berlin.

events.title: Bill Clinton becomes the first US president to visit Northern Ireland
events.description: Bill Clinton addressed crowds in Belfast and Derry in support of the peace process. The visit added momentum to the talks that produced the Good Friday Agreement in 1998.
